<span class="eyebrow">Structural repair</span>
<h1>Drain Pipe Replacement <span class="accent">Sydney</span></h1>
<p class="sh-lead">We replace Sydney drain and sewer lines that have collapsed, dropped out of fall or pulled apart at a joint, where no liner can restore the shape. Because it is the larger job, we only recommend it once the camera has shown why relining will not hold, and the price is agreed before we start. Book an assessment and find out which one your line needs.</p>
<div class="hh-acts"><a class="btn btn-red btn-lg" href="tel:0289600868"><svg class="ico ico-phone" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-phone"></use></svg> Request a drain pipe assessment</a><button class="btn btn-ghost btn-lg" type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="quickquote"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-file-lines"></use></svg> Get a Quick Quote</button></div>

</div>
<div class="symsel"><b>Relining is considered first</b><span>Replacement is for the cases a liner cannot answer.</span><ul>
<li><a href="/services/pipe-relining/"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-rotate"></use></svg><span>Cracked but still round</span><svg class="ico go" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-right"></use></svg></a></li>

<li><a href="/services/cctv-drain-inspection/"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-video"></use></svg><span>Not sure which</span><svg class="ico go" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-right"></use></svg></a></li>

<section class="section s-light"><div class="wrap"><figure class="figwide"><img src="/uploads/pipe-replacement-sydney.jpg" width="1536" height="864" alt="Open trench beside a brick wall with a new drain pipe going in and the broken clay sections lifted out alongside" loading="lazy" decoding="async" sizes="100vw"><figcaption>Replacement is the last option, not the first. The old clay comes out only once footage shows a liner cannot restore the shape.</figcaption></figure></div></section>
<section class="section s-white" aria-labelledby="first-title"><div class="wrap"><div class="callout"><span class="co-ic"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-rotate"></use></svg></span><div><h2 id="first-title">Relining is always considered first</h2><p>Replacing a drain line means excavating it, and on a Sydney property the cost usually sits in what is over the top rather than in the pipe. Driveways, paving, slabs and established gardens all have to be opened and reinstated.</p><p>So <a href="/services/pipe-relining/">pipe relining</a> is assessed first in every case, and replacement is recommended only where the footage shows a liner cannot work. If anyone quotes you a replacement without showing you why a liner will not hold, that is worth questioning.</p></div></div></div></section>
<section class="section s-light" id="when" aria-labelledby="when-title"><div class="wrap"><div class="head"><span class="eyebrow">When a liner will not hold</span><h2 id="when-title">When a line has to be replaced</h2><p class="lead">Five situations. The first three are the common ones, and all three are visible on camera rather than being matters of opinion.</p></div><div class="causes"><div class="cause is-struct"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-warning"></use></svg></span><div><h3>The pipe has collapsed</h3><p>A caved-in section cannot be lined, because there is no longer a host pipe for a liner to press against. The camera usually cannot pass it either, which is itself the answer.</p></div></div><div class="cause is-struct"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-trowel"></use></svg></span><div><h3>A section has dropped and lost its fall</h3><p>Drains rely on gravity. Where the ground has settled and a length of pipe now sits lower than the run either side, solids collect at the low point and the line blocks there repeatedly. data.name: Drain Pipe Replacement Sydney
data.description: Drain and sewer pipe replacement across Sydney for collapsed, dropped or misaligned lines that cannot be relined.

data.name: Drain pipe replacement
data.description: Excavation and replacement of collapsed, dropped or misaligned drain and sewer pipe across Sydney, where trenchless relining cannot restore the line.

mainEntity.name: How do I know the pipe actually needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the camera shows it. A line that is cracked but still round can almost always be relined, and that is the cheaper and less disruptive answer. Replacement becomes the right call when the pipe has collapsed, dropped out of fall, or is so misaligned a liner cannot pass. If you have been told a line needs replacing and have not seen footage showing one of those, ask for it.

mainEntity.name: How much of my garden will be dug up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only the length that has failed, in most cases. The line is traced and the depth confirmed first precisely so the opening can be kept to the failed section rather than opening a trench along the whole run. Where a line runs under a driveway or a slab, that is usually the strongest argument for relining instead, and it is considered first for exactly that reason.

mainEntity.name: Do you reinstate the surface afterwards?

acceptedAnswer.text: The excavation is backfilled and the surface made good. What reinstating involves depends on what was over the top, and that is set out in the quote before the work starts rather than discovered afterwards.

Neither is better. They answer different problems. A liner repairs a pipe that still holds its shape. Replacement renews a pipe that does not. Where both are genuinely possible, relining is usually less disruptive and less expensive once reinstating the surface is counted. Where the line has collapsed or lost its fall, relining is not an option at any price.

mainEntity.name: Can you replace just one section?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and that is the usual job. Replacing a whole line is only sensible where the camera shows the run is failing along its length rather than at one point.
